neighbours.label: the 'er'/'ers' piece right after a word-starting 'pass' in passer / passers / passersby / passerine, in any sense (football passer, people walking by, songbirds); not 'pass', 'passing', 'passed', 'passenger' or 'passport'
fire: The quarterback is the best passer in the league this season.
Passersby stopped to watch the street musician.
A passer on the sidewalk picked up the dropped wallet.
Sparrows and finches are both passerine birds.
Several passers-by called for an ambulance.
She was known as a gifted passer of the ball in midfield.
The mural caught the eye of every passerby on the corner.
Ornithologists counted dozens of passerines at the feeder.
quiet: The quarterback can pass the ball better than anyone in the league this season.
People walking by stopped to watch the street musician.
A pedestrian on the sidewalk picked up the dropped wallet.
Sparrows and finches are both perching songbirds.
Several people passing by called for an ambulance.
She was known for her passing of the ball in midfield.
neighbours.notes: Test sentences written blind by a second author who saw only the label (letsplay stream). Probing: prose ' pass', 'passing', 'passed', 'passenger', 'passport', 'passive', 'trespasser' all stayed under 0.07; 'passable'/'passably' fired 0.30-0.37 on the suffix piece (left out of the label as weaker). Corpus top examples are dominated by Python 'pass' statements and one 'Passover', which short probes did not reproduce (context/tokenization dependent); the inverse-DE solver flagged a leak on 'passing'/'pass' text that the resident probe scorer did not reproduce.
